findings.title: During Calendar Year 2008, Changes Were Made to Critical Provisions of MAIF’s Employee Bonus Program, without Which the Majority of the $1.4 Million in Bonuses Paid for the Year Would Not Have Been Paid
findings.description: The Board of Trustees approved changes to critical requirements of the bonus program allowing payment of approximately $1.4 million in bonuses that would not have been paid otherwise. The auditors question the timing and appropriateness given a net loss of $19.6 million.

dollar_amounts.context: bonuses paid for the year
bonuses based on non-financial performance results without changes
payments to management and executive employees
net loss incurred by MAIF

findings.recommendation: We recommend that the Board of Trustees not significantly revise or waive critical requirements of the bonus program to allow for the payment of bonuses after the requirements have been approved and the applicable year has begun.

findings.title: Certain Expenditures Should Be Disclosed to the Legislative Budget Committees as Part of the Annual Budget Submission Process
findings.description: Expenditures for consulting, marketing, lobbying, and outreach appeared inconsistent with MAIF's mission. The auditors recommend disclosure to legislative budget committees to ensure consistency with intended purpose.

dollar_amounts.context: strategic consulting services
marketing, public relations, and advertising
lobbying services
catering and space rental for producer appreciation events
corporate sponsorships

findings.recommendation: We recommend that MAIF report the detailed budget and expenditure data for consulting and lobbying services, marketing and public relations costs, as well as expenditures for producer related events, corporate sponsorships, and other similar outreach costs, to the legislative budget committees.

findings.title: Certain Procurement Transactions Were Not Consistent with MAIF’s Established Procedures
findings.description: Written documentation justifying sole source procurement was missing for three contracts totaling $287,000. Additionally, no written contract existed for maintenance services where payments totaled approximately $20,000.

dollar_amounts.context: service agreements with purchase orders issued
expenditures for contracts without sole source justification
payments to vendor for maintenance services

findings.recommendation: We recommend that MAIF a. maintain documentation justifying use of the sole source procurement method, and b. ensure written contracts are established with all vendors providing ongoing services.

findings.title: Sufficient Documentation to Support Expenditures Was Not Always on File or Properly Reviewed
findings.description: Detailed supporting receipts were not on file for $14,100 of credit card expenditures reviewed. Additionally, vendor invoices were not reviewed by fiscal personnel for $22,000 in other expenditures.

dollar_amounts.context: credit card expenditures reviewed
expenditures without detailed supporting receipts
total credit card expenditures in calendar year 2008
other MAIF expenditures reviewed
expenditures processed without reviewing vendor invoice

findings.recommendation: We recommend that a. MAIF require detailed receipts to support credit card expenditures, and b. fiscal personnel responsible for processing expenditures examine approved vendor invoices to help verify the accuracy and propriety of those expenditures.

findings.title: Certain Payments to Plaintiff Attorneys Were Not Reported in Accordance with Internal Revenue Service Regulations
findings.description: Form 1099 was not issued for five payments totaling approximately $100,000 due to incomplete vendor coding. Similar issues may affect an additional $560,000 in payments.

dollar_amounts.context: payments to plaintiff attorneys tested
payments lacking complete vendor coding information
total attorney payments by the Division for the year

findings.recommendation: We recommend that MAIF a. ensure that vendor coding information is properly recorded and that all applicable payments to plaintiff attorneys are reported as required by IRS regulations; and b. determine if previous payments not reported on Form 1099, such as those noted in our test work, need to be reported and, if so, report these previous payments to the IRS.
